questions.prompt: Why is epidemiology alone insufficient for dietary causation claims?
choices: A It always proves causation perfectly.
B It mainly shows correlation; confounders and absolute vs relative risk complicate headlines.
C Randomized trials never exist in nutrition.
D Correlation equals causation by definition.
questions.explain: Distinguish correlation from causation and how nutrition evidence is generated.

B Has very little impact on blood cholesterol; limited bioavailability.
C Is the only driver of heart disease.
D Must be zero always.

questions.prompt: Unhealthy fats in the population diet often come more from:
choices: A Plain steaks and grilled fish alone.
B Mixed dishes like pizza, fast-food burgers, and lasagnas—not simply whole steaks.
C Only olive oil.
D Water.
questions.explain: Mixed and fast-food dishes supply most unhealthy fats.

questions.prompt: Plant defense compounds / hormetic phytochemicals are framed as:
choices: A Always pure toxins to avoid forever.
B Often beneficial low-dose stressors (symbiotic phyto-adaptation), though individuals vary.
C Identical to essential amino acids.
D Only found in animal liver.
questions.explain: Low-dose plant compounds can stimulate adaptive benefit.

questions.prompt: On obesity and genes he concludes:
choices: A Genes are the primary fixed cause with no behavioral response.
B Genes play a role but obesity is highly responsive to choices compared with some other conditions.
C Obesity never responds to diet.
D Only surgery matters.
questions.explain: Genes matter but are not primary; obesity is highly choice-responsive.
